evidence.quote: These exclusions left 47,750 men, each of whom accrued follow-up time beginning on the month of return of the baseline questionnaire and ending on the month of diagnosis of prostate cancer, month of death from other causes, or January 31, 2002, whichever came first.

From 1986 to the end of the study period, January 31, 2002, in 673,706 person years, we documented 3,544 incident prostate adenocarcinoma cases after excluding 71 cases (about 2% of total) of stage T1a cancers.

Multivariable relative risks and 95% confidence intervals (in ()’s) for the high category versus low or reference category for selected variables from Cox models separately for total prostate cancer incidence and fatal prostate cancer in the Health Professionals Follow-Up Study.

Only 4 factors had a statistically significant association with incident prostate cancer: higher tomato sauce intake was associated with a decreased risk, and African–American race, a positive family history of prostate cancer, and higher α-linolenic acid intake were associated with an increased risk.

evidence.quote: Serum collected at study entry was available for 692 (86.2%) cases and 844 (88.9%) controls.

cases.excerpt: We examined whether serum concentrations of retinol were associated with the risk of prostate cancer in a nested case-control study using 692 prostate cancer cases and 844 matched controls from the Prostate, Lung, Colorectal, and Ovarian Cancer Screening Trial.

evidence.quote: Among the 347 prostate cancer cases who reported their dietary habits, 214 were diagnosed before and 133 after completing the FFQ.

In a sensitivity analysis we used logistic regression models to calculate ORs and 95% CIs of prostate cancer for rye- and oatmeal consumption in early life for incident cases only, adjusting for the same covariates as was done in the third model.

Compared with men consuming rye bread less than once per day, the OR in the multivariate model for total prostate cancer was 0.82 (95% CI: 0.56-1.20) and 0.73 (95% CI: 0.32-1.68) for advanced disease among men with high rye bread consumption in adolescence.
We compared men who were high (daily or more) and low (less than daily) consumers of rye bread in early life and midlife.

evidence.quote: In total, this left 114,217 participants who completed ≥2 (maximum 5) valid 24-h dietary assessments, of which 51,278 were men and 62,939 were women.
When breast cancer was the outcome of interest, models were restricted to women, and when prostate cancer was the outcome, models were restricted to men.
After a median of 9.4 years of follow-up, 1193 colorectal, 2024 female breast, and 2422 prostate cancer cases were identified.

When we looked at total grams of all dairy products, milk, and cheese we found no association with prostate cancer risk, whereas the latest WCRF meta-analysis of prospective studies from 2014 found that intakes of total grams of all dairy products, milk, and cheese were all associated with a higher risk of prostate cancer [6, 7, 56].
Hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CI) were estimated using multivariable-adjusted Cox regression.

adjudication.reason: Total dairy intake and prostate cancer were analyzed, supporting inclusion and the male analytical N. Its numerical results are unavailable in the supplied supplementary-figure text. A instead gives the continuous dairy-protein estimate; B gives a milk-protein quartile estimate and incorrect whole-cohort N. Neither supplies the requested total dairy association.

evidence.quote: In total, this left 114,217 participants who completed ≥2 (maximum 5) valid 24-h dietary assessments, of which 51,278 were men and 62,939 were women.
When breast cancer was the outcome of interest, models were restricted to women, and when prostate cancer was the outcome, models were restricted to men.
After a median of 9.4 years of follow-up, 1193 colorectal, 2024 female breast, and 2422 prostate cancer cases were identified.

When we looked at total grams of all dairy products, milk, and cheese we found no association with prostate cancer risk, whereas the latest WCRF meta-analysis of prospective studies from 2014 found that intakes of total grams of all dairy products, milk, and cheese were all associated with a higher risk of prostate cancer [6, 7, 56].
Hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CI) were estimated using multivariable-adjusted Cox regression.

cases.excerpt: We studied the associations between selenium exposure and prostate diseases such as prostate cancer (PCa) and benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH), and estimated the optimal range of selenium concentrations that may be needed to prevent these diseases among Nigerian men. Blood and urine samples from men with histologically diagnosed PCa (n = 90), BPH (n = 97), and controls (n = 98) were analyzed for trace elements, including selenium.

cases.excerpt: We studied the associations between selenium exposure and prostate diseases such as prostate cancer (PCa) and benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH), and estimated the optimal range of selenium concentrations that may be needed to prevent these diseases among Nigerian men. Blood and urine samples from men with histologically diagnosed PCa (n = 90), BPH (n = 97), and controls (n = 98) were analyzed for trace elements, including selenium.

design.excerpt: This case-control study was designed to investigate the mediating effects of environmental and lifestyle factors on PCa and BPH in men living in South-Eastern Nigeria.

The underlying case-control study is scientifically eligible, but the atomic contrast remains unresolved.
